fda-device-z-0201-2027.title: ROTOR ASSY-SW40 recall (Beckman Coulter, Inc.)
fda-device-z-0201-2027.product: ROTOR ASSY-SW40, Reference Number 331302, when the rotors are installed in the following centrifuges: Optima XPN-100 (Model Numbers A99846 and A94469), Optima XPN-90 (Model Numbers A99842 and A94468), Optima XPN-80 (Model Numbers A99839 and A95765), Optima XE-100 (Model Numbers A99836 and A94516), and Optima XE-90 (Model Numbers A99833 and A94471)
fda-device-z-0201-2027.reason: Optima XE XPN ultracentrifuge rotors may contain a microstructure defect that can cause rotors to break into two or more pieces (bifurcate) during a centrifugation run, resulting in destruction of samples being processed. When used for in vitro diagnostic (IVD) sample preparation, rotor breakage may delay patient test results. Additionally, sample destruction may expose laboratory personnel to biohazardous materials.

fda-device-z-0202-2027.title: ROTOR ASSY-SW41 recall (Beckman Coulter, Inc.)
fda-device-z-0202-2027.product: ROTOR ASSY-SW41, Reference Number 331362, when the rotors are installed in the following centrifuges: Optima XPN-100 (Model Numbers A99846 and A94469), Optima XPN-90 (Model Numbers A99842 and A94468), Optima XPN-80 (Model Numbers A99839 and A95765), Optima XE-100 (Model Numbers A99836 and A94516), and Optima XE-90 (Model Numbers A99833 and A94471)
fda-device-z-0202-2027.reason: Rotors have been found with a non-conforming microstructure, which may result in some rotors breaking into two or more pieces during use. Rotors that break into multiple pieces during use may result in significant damage to materials (i.e., samples) being processed in the centrifuge and to the centrifuge instrument.

fda-device-z-0203-2027.title: CareLink Clinic recall (Medtronic MiniMed, Inc.)
fda-device-z-0203-2027.reason: CareLink Clinic software version 4.4A includes a software defect in the Settings Calculator feature in which the calculation logic fails to use custom values entered by healthcare professionals (HCPs) for Total Daily Dose (TDD) or Long-acting insulin when calculating the Carb Ratio, Insulin Sensitivity Factor (ISF), and Max Recommended value for Rapid-acting insulin. Instead, the calculator continues to use the system-recommended values, resulting in incorrect rapid-acting insulin parameters. If an HCP or patient inputs these incorrect setting values into the patient's MiniMed Go app, the patient could deliver higher or lower insulin doses compared to their insulin needs, potentially leading to over/under delivery of insulin with a severity ranging from Catastrophic (death from severe hypoglycemia) to Minor (self-treatable hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia).
fda-device-z-0203-2027.distribution: US Nationwide distribution in the state of KS.
fda-device-z-0203-2027.codes: UDI-DI: 0763000B00008748K.  Software Versions: 4.4A  Software Available: US: Between June 4th, 2026, and June 8th, 2026.

This product is not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for extended wear use.

fda-device-z-0208-2027.title: Automated Impella Controller recall (Abiomed, Inc.)
fda-device-z-0208-2027.product: Automated Impella Controller, Packaged. Primary user control interface for the Impella Catheter, catheter-based heart pump.
fda-device-z-0208-2027.reason: Retrospective review of servicing records identified AIC units requiring various hardware, firmware, and/or software update(s):  1. RFID firmware issue that may result in failure of the AIC to recognize the purge cassette during case setup or cassette change. This issue may result in delay in procedure or therapy.   2. Potential for the rotary push button (RPB) sticking and unreliable actuation impacting operator ability to select and confirm menu entries. This can result in loss of control of the console.   3. Potential AIC instability that could result in AIC start-up failure, inability to drive the pump, and the need for console exchange.   4. Software defect related to calculator process crash, leading to Negative Central Venous Pressure (CVP) values present in Pulmonary Artery Pressure (PAP) calculations.

fda-device-z-0264-2027.title: Generic Name: restor3d MTP Implant  Generic Name: MTP Implant  Model/Catalog Number:... recall (restor3d Inc.)
fda-device-z-0264-2027.product: Generic Name: restor3d MTP Implant  Generic Name: MTP Implant  Model/Catalog Number: 1103-161620  Software Version: None  Product Description: The restor3d Metatarsophalangeal (MTP) Implant is a sterile, single-use implant grade metal device, available in varied articulating surface coverages. The restor3d MTP implant is designed to replace the damaged articulating surface of the first metatarsal distal head. The device is intended for the treatment of patients with degenerative and post-traumatic arthritis in the first metatarsal joint in the presence of good bone stock and integrity of the first metatarsal head. This implant can also be used in the following clinical conditions: hallux valgus or hallux limitus, hallux rigidus, and an unstable or painful metatarsal/phalangeal (MTP) joint. The implant is a single use product intended to be press fit, with optional use of bone cement. The restor3d MTP Implant is comprised of a single laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) printed cobalt-chromium alloy (Co28Cr6Mo) part. The external surface of the implant that is intended to be in contact with the phalanx is mirror polished.  Component: Not a component
fda-device-z-0264-2027.reason: Implants were found in the field with orange sterilzation indicators which means implants were not exposed to sterilization.
fda-device-z-0264-2027.distribution: U.S. Nationwide distribution in the states of FL, IL, NC, PA, SC, and TX.

fda-device-z-0265-2027.title: Generic Name: MiniMed Go App  Generic Name: MiniMed Go App  Model/Catalog Number: MMT-8600 recall (Medtronic MiniMed, Inc.)
fda-device-z-0265-2027.product: Generic Name: MiniMed Go App  Generic Name: MiniMed Go App  Model/Catalog Number: MMT-8600 (iOS), MMT-8601 (Android)  Software Version: Software version 1.2.1  Product Description: The MiniMed Go app for iOS or MiniMed Go app for Android is compatible with the following  components:  " Simplera sensor  " Instinct sensor  " InPen smart insulin pen  " Apple Watch [Optional]    Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a technology that allows you to continuously view  glucose values. The app uses an inserted Simplera sensor CGM or Instinct sensor CGM with  Bluetooth¿ wireless technology that converts small amounts of glucose from the interstitial fluid  under the skin into an electronic signal. The sensors use that signal to provide sensor glucose (SG)  values to the MiniMed Go app on a compatible mobile device.    The app also provides alerts based on your SG levels and contains a user interface for entering data  such as insulin, meals, exercise, blood glucose (BG) values, and uploading information to the  CareLink" Personal website.  The app is available to download from the Apple"* App Store"* or the Google Play"* Store.  Component: No
fda-device-z-0265-2027.reason: A software defect in which existing users who had previously configured and enabled the long-acting dose reminder feature in version 1.2.0 or earlier experienced failure of the long-acting dose reminder after updating their app to version 1.2.1. The long-acting dose reminder is an optional feature that, when enabled, triggers a notification at the scheduled time to remind users to take their long-acting insulin dose. The issue was caused by a type cast exception during database migration that occurs upon app update to version 1.2.1 causing a silent failure that prevented the creation of new alerts. Failure to receive the long-acting dose reminder may result in missed or delayed insulin doses, potentially leading to hyperglycemia. Conversely, if users are uncertain whether they took their dose due to the missing reminder, inadvertent duplicate dosing may occur, potentially resulting in hypoglycemia.

fda-device-z-0311-2027.title: Nalu TD2 Therapy Disc with firmware recall (Boston Scientific Neuromodulation Corporation)
fda-device-z-0311-2027.product: Nalu TD2 Therapy Disc with firmware, REF: 34014-001, and TD2 Patient Kit, REF: 74011, part of the Nalu Neurostimulation System
fda-device-z-0311-2027.reason: Therapy Disc (TD) that powers and sends stimulation signals to an Implantable Pulse Generator (IPG), part of a neurostimulation system, has a firmware issue that causes the TD to attempt to restart, then fail, leading it to become non-functional, and if a secondary TD is unavailable, this may lead IPG to become non-functional, thus unable to inhibit transmission of pain signals.
fda-device-z-0311-2027.distribution: US Nationwide distribution in the states of PA, FL, OR, AZ, OH, SC, TX, OR, OK, MI, CA, NJ.

fda-device-z-0314-2027.title: Precision Pointer Electromagnetic recall (Stryker Leibinger GmbH & Co. KG)
fda-device-z-0314-2027.reason: Device may fracture during use at the laser welded joint on the pointer tube. If this happens, loose parts may fall out of the product while the device is inside the patient.
fda-device-z-0314-2027.distribution: Worldwide - US Nationwide distribution in the states of Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, Montana, New Hampshire, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Washington and the countries of Austria, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Japan,  Norway, Portugal, South Korea, Spain, Switzerland, UK.

fda-device-z-0315-2027.title: Carevo recall (ARJOHUNTLEIGH POLSKA Sp. z.o.o.)
fda-device-z-0315-2027.product: Carevo, Height-adjustable shower trolley, Model Number BAC1111-01
fda-device-z-0315-2027.reason: The side support of the shower trolley may open unintentionally when the handles are not fully locked and additional force is applied during patient handling. If the side support is not fully locked and an additional force is applied by the caregiver on the handle (e.g., during turning or repositioning), the panel may open unintentionally, which can lead to a resident/patient fall and serious injury, such as head injury, fractures, or other trauma resulting from a patient fall.
